headlines.title: All U.S. bombers leave UK air base on concerns of suspected terror plots; more tankers struck near Iran in the Middle East
headlines.summary: Tankers getting hit near Iran while U.S. bombers are repositioning — that's not background noise, that's the tape screaming. Energy names, defense contractors, and shipping stocks all move on this; oil supply disruption risk through the Strait of Hormuz is the kind of thing that reprices the whole energy complex overnight. The Aramco CEO already warned it could take two years to rebuild global oil inventories — this headline pours gasoline on that fire.

headlines.title: Traders Are Dusting Off The Contagion Playbook for European Bonds
headlines.summary: When the Street starts pulling out the contagion playbook, you pay attention — we've seen this movie before and it doesn't end well. The euro hitting a 17-month low, Spain calling a snap election, and French fiscal jitters all hitting at once is a recipe for a risk-off session that bleeds into U.S. Treasuries, financials, and multinationals with European exposure. This is the kind of macro backdrop that can turn a garden-variety selloff into something uglier.

headlines.title: Musk hints TSMC may join his mega chip venture, and Intel's stock is taking a hit
headlines.summary: Musk dangling TSMC's name into his Terafab story is a direct gut-punch to Intel, which has been desperately trying to sell itself as the domestic foundry champion — if TSMC is in the mix, Intel's whole strategic narrative takes a hit. This reshuffles the AI chip supply chain story and touches NVDA, AMD, and the broader semiconductor complex. Single-name impact on INTC is immediate; the ripple effects on the foundry pecking order are worth watching all week.
